headline: Rain arrives late tonight into Saturday morning, then cooler, mostly dry weather follows into early next week, with a weak front possible midweek.
summary: The warm, dry spell ended Friday as a ridge of high pressure (a zone of higher pressure aloft) moved east, letting a trough (a dip in the jet stream) and a front move in from the west. Forecasters expect most of the rain late Friday night into early Saturday morning, mainly along the coast and in the mountains. After the front passes, a convergence zone (a band where air flowing around the Olympics and Cascades comes together and lifts) is expected to set up along the Snohomish/King county line, which could bring lingering showers there. Saturday's highs cool to the upper 50s to lower 60s. Sunday is cooler and dry for most places, with a few showers lingering in the Cascades and highs in the upper 50s. Next week looks mostly dry. A low-pressure system off the coast Monday should barely clip the area, with at most a shower or two along the coast. Tuesday brings light offshore (easterly) winds and highs in the upper 50s. A weak front may bring a chance of rain from Wednesday into Thursday, and that part is less certain. There are no watches, warnings, or advisories for land areas. Boaters should note Small Craft Advisories on Saturday for westerly winds in the Strait of Juan de Fuca and for waves around 10 feet on the outer coastal waters.
changes: The forecast stayed consistent on the Friday night to Saturday rain, but the afternoon and evening updates trimmed the Monday system, saying it will barely clip the area, and cooled Saturday's highs slightly. Later updates also dropped the earlier Saturday afternoon sunbreak and morning-low details for Sunday and added a Small Craft Advisory for the outer coastal waters in the evening.
